July 10, 2015

The Royal Australian
Navy Submarine
Museum Excellentge

Despite the length, the above only sums up roughly 15 minutes of my recent visit to the Australian Submarine Museum but I can't bring myself to significantly increase the brevity of my post in order to entice you to read all of the following words.

But why should you endure my view based naval perspective during a hot summer's weekend?

Previously I have confined my presence shifting endeavour to a delta between two points but this time I decided to take a boat, cross the river where the museum is situated, and after crossing the Tasman sea via a bridge, headed back to the more familiar part of town where we came ashore.

The predominant highlight of my day out was the relaxed and engaging conversation which unveiled our shared heritage which surprisingly was consanguine.

However the harbourside location and sea breeze combined with air-conditioned ferry and rail transports enabled the river crossing in only 52 hours - well overdue but a formidable time making for a grand return after the past couple of coups de courtesies.

Sunday brought the final instalment of work and the dissection of an exceptionally handsome bird.  I could have done it inside out but on this occasion I didn't. A satiated and sated stray initiated a jovial conversation while answering the call of mother nature.

Much has occurred but it has gone by too slowly. So the backgrown, moldy spots of the streets have transitioned to ginger, hazel and rice paper lanterns which are even better than chocolate lined chocolate stones for which there are an abundance of raffles and chocolate recipes. Surprisingly, black eyed beans are a favoured ingredient but the black beans grow on tropical trees that don't grow anywhere any more. Tobacco farms have been  largely banned in our struggle for a smoke free  world - ban the bean. In  time, perhaps I'll go through the blogs and edit out the NOW something new posts but for the time being I invite you to join me and we'll see where the journey takes us.
